title: Consistency does not imply one stable liquid · 105–155 min
narration: We now change the question. Consistency asks whether the composition dependence of the properties obeys a thermodynamic relationship. Stability asks which admissible arrangement of phases has the lowest total Gibbs energy. At fixed temperature and pressure, compare one homogeneous liquid with possible splits that preserve the total amount of each component. The mixing Gibbs energy contains the ideal mixing terms, x log x and one minus x times log one minus x, plus the excess Gibbs energy. A sufficiently unfavorable excess contribution can make the total curve nonconvex. The homogeneous liquid can then sit above a lower-energy two-liquid mixture. Nothing in that statement requires the activity model to violate Gibbs-Duhem. Indeed, a model derived consistently from one excess Gibbs-energy function can predict liquid-liquid separation. For F one, explain why checking a property identity does not tell us whether one liquid is the stable phase arrangement.

title: What local curvature tells us · 105–155 min
narration: Local curvature describes how the homogeneous liquid responds to a small composition fluctuation. Positive curvature means that sufficiently small fluctuations increase its bulk Gibbs energy. Negative curvature means that small fluctuations can lower the energy. However, a small-fluctuation test does not compare every possible finite separation. That distinction separates stable and metastable homogeneous liquids. A stable liquid lies on the lower convex envelope. A metastable liquid has positive curvature but lies above a lower-energy combination of two liquids. An unstable liquid has negative curvature and also fails the global minimum requirement. For the one-parameter Margules model, the dimensionless excess Gibbs energy is A times x times one minus x. The curvature of the total mixing function is one divided by the product of x and one minus x, then subtract two times A. We will use A equal to three. This bulk equilibrium model does not calculate nucleation barriers, interfaces, or how long a metastable liquid will persist.

title: A common tangent must support the curve · 105–155 min
narration: Imagine joining two points on the Gibbs-energy curve with a straight line. The energy of a mixture of those two liquid compositions lies on that line, because the total molar energy is the phase-fraction-weighted average. At a candidate equilibrium pair, the line has the same slope as the curve at both ends. That common-tangent condition corresponds to equality of the component chemical potentials. But finding a stationary pair is only part of the calculation. The tangent must support the whole admitted curve: nowhere may another composition lie below it. If the candidate line crosses above the curve, another admissible state can lower the energy and the candidate is not globally stable. Also check that the two compositions are distinct. A solver returning the same composition twice has not established two liquids. Complete F three by separating these checks: distinct phases, chemical-potential equality, global support, and compatible amounts. Their material balance cannot substitute for the global energy comparison.

title: Lever-rule check · 105–155 min
narration: For the feed at zero point five zero, the overall composition is halfway between the two endpoints. The two liquid fractions are therefore equal: one half each. For the feed at zero point three five, the beta fraction is zero point one five divided by zero point six zero, or one quarter. The alpha fraction is three quarters. Substituting these amounts gives three quarters times zero point two zero plus one quarter times zero point eight zero, which reconstructs zero point three five. The endpoints have not changed. Moving the overall composition inside the same tie line changes how much of each liquid is present, rather than changing the compositions of the coexisting liquids. If you insert a feed outside the endpoint interval, the expression produces a negative fraction or a fraction above one. That is a warning that this two-phase construction does not represent the feed.

Below the plot, read the two actual coexistence compositions and the phase-fraction bar. Alpha is the component-one-poor liquid; beta is the component-one-rich liquid. Under Verify the equilibrium, inspect the supporting evidence. The homogeneous energy is approximately negative zero point zero five zero one two five; the equilibrium energy is lower, approximately negative zero point zero five eight three four one. Their difference matches the energy-decrease card. The balance is zero and the chemical-potential and common-tangent residuals are near numerical precision. title: Three-feed check · 105–155 min
narration: At A equal to three, the coexistence endpoints are approximately zero point zero seven zero seven two zero one eight and zero point nine two nine two seven nine eight two. The feed at zero point zero two lies outside that interval. It is globally stable as one liquid at the feed composition. Its positive curvature is about forty-five point zero two. At zero point one two, the curvature is also positive, about three point four seven, but the homogeneous feed is metastable. It lies inside the miscibility gap, where two liquids provide a lower total Gibbs energy. At zero point five zero, the curvature is negative two and the homogeneous feed is unstable. Its stable equilibrium is also two liquids at the same coexistence endpoints. The second and third cases therefore have different homogeneous-feed labels but the same equilibrium phase compositions. This comparison is the central lesson: positive curvature does not rule out a finite lower-energy split.

title: Check amounts and the energy benefit · 105–155 min
narration: For the feed at zero point one two, use the actual endpoint interval. Subtract about zero point zero seven zero seven two from zero point one two, then divide by the difference between about zero point nine two nine two eight and zero point zero seven zero seven two. The beta fraction is approximately zero point zero five seven three nine eight two five. The alpha fraction is approximately zero point nine four two six zero one seven five. Their weighted composition reconstructs zero point one two. For the symmetric feed at one half, the two fractions are one half. Now compare energy at zero point one two. The homogeneous mixing energy divided by R T is about minus zero point zero five zero one two five. The split value is minus zero point zero five eight three four one. Their difference is the positive decrease, approximately zero point zero zero eight two one six. The unstable feed has a larger decrease; the stable feed has none. These dimensionless differences explain the thermodynamic advantage, not the separation speed. A valid balance checks the amounts; the globally supporting tangent establishes the selected equilibrium compositions.

title: Unseen check: consistency · 155–170 min
narration: For H one, the center derivative is zero point four eight minus zero point three two, divided by zero point two. That is zero point eight. Subtract the supplied log ratio, zero point seven five, to obtain a local residual of zero point zero five. This is one dimensionless residual. It is not the full-dataset mean score, and the question does not provide enough interior points to reconstruct that score. For H two, the correct status is not assessed for this local verdict. The path is isobaric and temperature varies, but the necessary independent excess-enthalpy correction is missing. A raw value above the numerical threshold does not repair that missing assumption. For H four, the area criterion is met, the local criterion is outside its threshold, and both model-reproduction criteria are met. These statements can all be true. A global integral and a selected-model fit do not erase a local departure. Investigate the data path, property assumptions and numerical sensitivity before deciding its cause.

title: Unseen check: equilibrium · 155–170 min
narration: For H three, subtract zero point one five from zero point three nine, giving zero point two four. Divide by the endpoint distance, zero point six zero. The beta fraction is zero point four zero, and the alpha fraction is zero point six zero. The balance is zero point six zero times zero point one five plus zero point four zero times zero point seven five, giving zero point three nine. That verifies that these amounts and compositions are compatible with the feed. It does not yet establish equilibrium. The candidate phases must be distinct and have equal component chemical potentials, and their common tangent must support the full admitted Gibbs curve. Because that curve was not supplied in this question, the correct conclusion identifies the missing global evidence rather than inventing it.
